newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW--US Jan trade gap rose to $10.29 bln.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW--US Jan trade gap rose to $10.29 bln.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department reported the international trade deficit in December expanded to $10.29 billion from a revised $7.94 billion in November.
Economists had expected an increase to $9.9 billion.

EVELINA TAINER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, INDOSUEZ CARR FUTURES: "It's in line with the numbers that the Commerce Department was also expecting when they put together the GDP estimate for the fourth quarter. So it does mean pretty minor revisions to the GDP component."

JOHN RYDING, MANAGING DIRECTOR AND SENIOR ECONOMIST, BEAR STEARNS & CO INC: This number is nothing exciting. Combined with the downward revision to November's deficit, this data was about what the Commerce Department assumed in its fourth quarter GDP report. There continues to be this odd bias in trade deficit, in which it narrows in fourth quarter and widens in the first quarter. On a month to month basis, the data is too distorted to identify underlying trends.

KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "Let's watch what happens to the dollar ... You could see some pressure on the greenback and that could limit or stem some enthusiasm from the (Consumer Price Index) CPI report, at least from a foreign investor perspective."
RAM BHAGAVATULA, CHIEF FINANCIAL ECONOMIST, CITICORP SECRITIES MARKETS INC:
"Trade was as expected; there's really no big mysteries. What it says is fourth-quarter GDP is likely to be revised down because exports are not as strong as assumed."
